title.en: Delaunay tetrahedra and the empty sphere property

summary: Partition space around a point set and let the defining empty-sphere condition be tested rather than assumed.
objective: Build a Delaunay tetrahedralisation where selecting a cell shows its circumscribing sphere and confirms that no other vertex lies inside it.
intent_signals: Show how a set of points partitions space into tetrahedra.
Test the empty sphere property on a cell I select.
example_prompts: Build a 3D Delaunay triangulation with selectable cells and their circumscribing spheres.
Show what happens to the triangulation when five points become cospherical.
negative_signals: Not a meshing pipeline for simulation: element quality, refinement and boundary conformity are out of scope.
Not a Voronoi diagram recipe; the dual is only referenced, not asserted here.
not_for: Not a meshing pipeline for simulation: element quality, refinement and boundary conformity are out of scope.
Not a Voronoi diagram recipe; the dual is only referenced, not asserted here.

entities.name: Vertex set
entities.guidance: Give editable points stable IDs. In the full-dimensional case the boundary of the finite-cell union is the convex-hull surface, whose facets deserve their own highlight; it is not the boundary of the finite point set itself.

entities.name: Tetrahedral cells
entities.guidance: Show cells as separable tetrahedra with shared faces, able to be exploded outward without losing adjacency information.

entities.name: Circumsphere probe
entities.guidance: Offer the circumscribing sphere only for finite, full-dimensional tetrahedra. Infinite cells have no meaningful circumsphere, and when the point set drops below three dimensions the probe is disabled and the rank drop is reported instead.

state_contract.model: Point list, a triangulation recomputed after edits, per-cell adjacency including the infinite cells used as boundary scaffolding, the current triangulation dimension, and an empty-sphere test with a stated tolerance evaluated only on finite full-dimensional cells from canonical un-exploded coordinates. Ties in near-cospherical configurations are resolved by the implementation.
state_contract.authority: The triangulation structure is authoritative; exploded cell positions are display transforms that never alter adjacency.
actions: Select a cell and run its empty-sphere test.
Drag a vertex and watch cells flip.
Reset the point set and the explode amount.

invariants: Each face is incident to exactly two cells once infinite cells are counted; a convex hull facet is incident to one finite cell and one infinite cell, which is scaffolding rather than a drawable tetrahedron.
A reported empty-sphere test names its tolerance instead of implying exactness.
Exploding cells changes only their transforms, so collapsing the explode returns the exact original partition.
The union of the finite cells covers the convex hull of the point set, which is not the same thing as the point set itself.
A selected cell is invalidated when the triangulation is recomputed, and sphere geometry is always computed from canonical coordinates rather than from exploded display positions.
motion_guidance: Animate a cell flip when a vertex crosses a degenerate configuration; a silent retriangulation hides the most interesting event.
Keep explode motion radial from the centroid so adjacency stays visually traceable.
known_limits: Degenerate cospherical configurations have more than one valid triangulation; the one shown is whatever the implementation chooses.
No element quality metric is computed, so cells may be arbitrarily thin.
When the point set is coplanar or lower dimensional the triangulation dimension drops below three; the scene reports that state and disables the sphere probe rather than drawing degenerate cells.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Delaunay triangulations have the empty sphere property: the circumscribing sphere of each cell contains no other vertex of the triangulation in its interior.
claims.scope: Defining property of finite full-dimensional cells; floating-point tests are approximate and need a stated tolerance, and the property is not evaluated on infinite cells or on degenerate lower-dimensional configurations.

source_refs.locator: 3D Triangulations, Definition and Representation; Delaunay empty sphere property

claims.statement: The triangulation is uniquely defined except in degenerate cases such as five cospherical points, where an implementation may still return one particular triangulation.
claims.scope: Uniqueness caveat as documented for one library version.

claims.statement: Convex hull facets can be handled uniformly by attaching each to an infinite cell with an auxiliary infinite vertex, so every facet is incident to exactly two cells.
claims.scope: Documented representation choice for boundary handling, not a geometric property of the point set; the infinite vertex has no meaningful coordinates for geometric predicates.

source_refs.locator: 3D Triangulations, Representation and Degenerate Dimensions; infinite vertex and infinite cells

object_craft.structure: Solid tetrahedra with slightly inset faces so neighbouring cells remain visually separable when assembled.
object_craft.material: A single neutral material with per-cell value variation; reserve saturated colour for the selected cell and its circumsphere.
object_craft.articulation: Cells translate along the centroid direction under an explode parameter and return exactly on reset.

object_craft.structure: A thin wireframe sphere plus an opaque centre marker, sized from the selected cell only.
object_craft.material: Wire-only sphere so interior vertices stay visible; any vertex found inside is marked with a distinct failure badge.
object_craft.articulation: Rebuilt whenever the selection or the point set changes.

physical_contract.scope: Static geometric partition with display-only explode; no physics.
checks: Every interior face reports exactly two incident cells.
Explode set to zero reproduces the original vertex positions.
